plan.title: Kidney bulk RNA-seq treated vs control DE with batch adjustment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 12000-gene x 12-sample raw-count matrix (salmon gene-level counts) from human kidney tissue, with 6 treated vs 6 control samples processed across two known batches that are balanced across condition (3 treated + 3 control per batch). Because batch is balanced with respect to condition, it can be included as a covariate in the differential expression model without collinearity with the condition of interest, and a design-matrix based test (DESeq2 with ~batch+condition) is the correct approach — no surrogate-variable estimation is needed since batch is known and recorded. The plan: (1) load and QC-filter the raw counts and metadata, verifying the stated design (6v6, 2 batches balanced); (2) run DESeq2 with the two-covariate design to test condition while adjusting for batch, applying independent filtering and shrinkage-based log fold changes for a stable, ranked gene list; (3) run functional enrichment on the significant DE genes to interpret biological pathways affected by treatment, reporting gracefully if organism gene-set references are unavailable in this environment. Steps are ordered so QC/DE precedes interpretation, and each step declares the packages it needs so the executing agent can verify availability before running.
